             'small{color:#697383}@media(max-width:600px){main{margin:16px auto}h1{font-size:28px}}')
    with sqlite3.connect(database) as db:
        db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS items(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)")

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, *args):
            pass

        def send(self, status, body, kind="text/html; charset=utf-8"):
            parts = (body,) if isinstance(body, str) else body
            parts = tuple(part.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(part, str) else part for part in parts)
            size = sum(len(part) if isinstance(part, bytes) else part.seek(0, 2) for part in parts)
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", kind)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(size))
            self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
            self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
            self.end_headers()
            for part in parts:
                if isinstance(part, bytes):
                    self.wfile.write(part)
                else:
                    part.seek(0)
                    while chunk := part.read(8192):
                        self.wfile.write(chunk)

        def page(self, status, heading, content):
            parts = (content,) if isinstance(content, str) else content
            return self.send(status, ('<!doctype html><html lang="zh-CN"><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">'
                             '<title>' + html.escape(heading) + '</title><style>' + style + '</style><main><h1>' + html.escape(heading) + '</h1>', *parts, '</main></html>'))

        def edit_id(self, path):
            match = re.fullmatch(re.escape(prefix) + r'/items/([0-9]{1,19})/edit', path)
            if match and 0 < int(match[1]) <= 2**63 - 1:
                return int(match[1])

        def edit_page(self, item_id, raw_title, status=200, error=""):
            # The extra leading newline is consumed by HTML; preserve the user's first newline.
            value = html.escape(raw_title, quote=True).replace('\r', '') if isinstance(raw_title, str) else raw_title
            field = ('<label for="edit-title">事项标题</label><textarea id="edit-title" name="title" rows="2" maxlength="200" required' + (' readonly' if status == 404 else '') + (' aria-describedby="edit-error"' if error else '') + '>\n', value, '</textarea>')
            message = '<p id="edit-error" role="alert">' + html.escape(error) + '</p>' if error else ''
            back = '<a href="' + html.escape(prefix + '/', quote=True) + '">' + ('返回应用' if error else '取消') + '</a>'
            if status == 404:
                content = (message + '<div class="edit-form">', *field, back + '</div>')
            else:
                action = html.escape(prefix + '/items/%d/edit' % item_id, quote=True)
                content = (message + '<form class="edit-form" method="post" action="' + action + '"><input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="' + token + '">', *field, '<button>' + ('重试保存' if error else '保存') + '</button> ' + back + '</form>')
            return self.page(status, '编辑事项', content)

        def read_large_edit(self, remaining, title_file):
            # Keep only the first title/CSRF, like parse_qs(...)[0], without a large allocation.
            name, field, tail, csrf = b'', None, b'', ''
            seen = set()
            decoder = None
            while remaining:
                chunk = self.rfile.read(min(8192, remaining))
                if not chunk:
                    raise ValueError('incomplete form')
                remaining -= len(chunk)
                pieces = chunk.split(b'&')
                for index, piece in enumerate(pieces):
                    final = index < len(pieces) - 1 or remaining == 0
                    if field is None:
                        key, separator, piece = piece.partition(b'=')
                        # Even fully percent-encoded "title" is only 15 bytes long.
                        name = (name + key)[:16]
                        if not separator and not final:
                            continue
                        key = unquote_to_bytes(name.replace(b'+', b' '))
                        field = key if key in (b'title', b'csrf') and key not in seen else b''
                        seen.add(field)
                        decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')(errors='replace')
                    if field:
                        data, tail = tail + piece, b''
                        if not final:
                            last_percent = data.rfind(b'%')
                            if last_percent >= 0 and len(data) - last_percent < 3:
                                data, tail = data[:last_percent], data[last_percent:]
                        text = decoder.decode(unquote_to_bytes(data.replace(b'+', b' ')), final=final)
                        if field == b'title':
                            title_file.write(html.escape(text, quote=True).replace('\r', '').encode('utf-8'))
                        else:
                            csrf = (csrf + text)[:len(token) + 1]
                    if final:
                        name, field, tail = b'', None, b''
            return csrf

        def oversized_edit(self, item_id, size):
            # Rejected bodies never write items. Disk-backed recovery keeps memory bounded.
            with ExitStack() as cleanup:
                try:
                    title_file = cleanup.enter_context(tempfile.TemporaryFile())
                    csrf = self.read_large_edit(size, title_file)
                    title_file.flush()
                except OSError:
                    self.close_connection = True
                    back = html.escape(prefix + '/items/%d/edit' % item_id, quote=True)
                    return self.page(503, '暂时无法保留编辑内容', '<p>此次编辑未保存，未能保留完整输入。请返回编辑页重试。</p><a href="' + back + '">返回编辑页</a>')
                if not hmac.compare_digest(csrf.encode('utf-8'), token.encode('ascii')):
                    return self.edit_page(item_id, title_file, 403, '页面已过期，请确认内容后重试')
                try:
                    with sqlite3.connect(database) as db:
                        row = db.execute('SELECT id FROM items WHERE id=?', (item_id,)).fetchone()
                    if row is None:
                        return self.edit_page(item_id, title_file, 404, '事项不存在')
                except sqlite3.Error:
                    return self.edit_page(item_id, title_file, 503, '数据暂时不可用，请稍后重试；此次编辑尚未保存。')
                return self.edit_page(item_id, title_file, 413, '表单内容超过 8192 字节，事项应为 1 到 200 字；请修改后重试。')

        def unavailable(self):
            if urlsplit(self.path).path == prefix + "/health":
                return self.send(503, '{"status":"unavailable"}', "application/json")
            retry = ""
            if self.pending_save is not None:
                operation, item_id, raw_title = self.pending_save
                if operation == 'edit':
                    return self.edit_page(item_id, raw_title, 503, '数据暂时不可用，请稍后重试；此次编辑尚未保存。')
                retry = '<form method="post" action="' + html.escape(prefix + '/items', quote=True) + '"><input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="' + token + '"><label for="retry-title">未保存的内容</label><input id="retry-title" name="title" maxlength="200" value="' + html.escape(raw_title, quote=True) + '"><button>重试保存</button></form>'
            return self.page(503, '数据暂时不可用', '<p>请稍后重试，当前操作未完成。</p>' + retry + '<p><a href="' + html.escape(prefix + '/', quote=True) + '">返回应用</a></p>')

        def do_GET(self):
            self.pending_save = None
            try:
                return self.get()
            except sqlite3.Error:
                return self.unavailable()

        def get(self):
            path = urlsplit(self.path).path
            if path == prefix + "/health":
                with sqlite3.connect(database) as db:
                    db.execute("SELECT id FROM items LIMIT 1").fetchall()
                return self.send(200, '{"status":"ok"}', "application/json")
            item_id = self.edit_id(path)
            if item_id is not None:
                with sqlite3.connect(database) as db:
                    row = db.execute('SELECT title FROM items WHERE id=?', (item_id,)).fetchone()
                if row is None:
                    return self.edit_page(item_id, '', 404, '事项不存在')
                return self.edit_page(item_id, row[0])
            if path != prefix + "/":
                return self.send(404, "页面不存在")
            with sqlite3.connect(database) as db:
                rows = db.execute("SELECT id,title,done FROM items ORDER BY id DESC").fetchall()
            esc = html.escape
            items = "".join('<li><form method="post" action="%s/items/%d"><input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="%s"><span>%s</span><button name="done" value="%d">%s</button><a href="%s/items/%d/edit">编辑</a></form></li>' %
                            (esc(prefix, quote=True), i, token, esc(text), 0 if done else 1, "重新打开" if done else "完成", esc(prefix, quote=True), i) for i, text, done in rows)
            self.send(200, '<!doctype html><html lang="zh-CN"><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">'
                      '<title>' + esc(title) + '</title><style>' + style + '</style><main>'
                      '<small>WEB 应用起点</small><h1>' + esc(title) + '</h1><p>应用已经可以运行。先添加一项内容，刷新后仍会保留。具体业务能力将在交付流程中实现和验证。</p>'
                      '<form method="post" action="' + prefix + '/items"><input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="' + token + '"><label for="title">新事项</label><input id="title" name="title" required maxlength="200" placeholder="写下一件要做的事"><button>添加</button></form>'
                      '<ul>' + (items or '<li>还没有内容，添加第一项开始。</li>') + '</ul><p><small>仅用于本地开发；正式发布前需要按实际业务配置身份验证、数据保护和部署环境。</small></p></main></html>')

        def do_POST(self):
            self.pending_save = None
            try:
                return self.post()
            except sqlite3.Error:
                return self.unavailable()

        def post(self):
            path = urlsplit(self.path).path
            item_id = self.edit_id(path)
            try:
                n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
                if not 0 < n <= 8192:
                    if n > 8192 and item_id is not None:
                        return self.oversized_edit(item_id, n)
                    return self.send(413, "表单内容过大或为空")
                values = parse_qs(self.rfile.read(n).decode("utf-8"), keep_blank_values=True)
            except (ValueError, UnicodeError):
                return self.send(400, "表单格式错误")
            raw_title = values.get("title", [""])[0]
            if not hmac.compare_digest(values.get("csrf", [""])[0].encode("utf-8"), token.encode("ascii")):
                if item_id is not None:
                    return self.edit_page(item_id, raw_title, 403, '页面已过期，请确认内容后重试')
                return self.send(403, "页面已过期，请刷新后重试")
            if item_id is not None:
                self.pending_save = ('edit', item_id, raw_title)
            elif path.startswith(prefix + '/items/') and path.endswith('/edit'):
                return self.send(404, '事项不存在')
            elif path == prefix + '/items':
                self.pending_save = ('create', None, raw_title)
            with sqlite3.connect(database) as db:
                if item_id is not None:
                    if db.execute('SELECT id FROM items WHERE id=?', (item_id,)).fetchone() is None:
                        return self.edit_page(item_id, raw_title, 404, '事项不存在')
                    if not raw_title.strip() or len(raw_title) > 200:
                        return self.edit_page(item_id, raw_title, 400, '事项应为 1 到 200 字，不能全为空白')
                    cur = db.execute('UPDATE items SET title=? WHERE id=?', (raw_title, item_id))
                    if not cur.rowcount:
                        return self.edit_page(item_id, raw_title, 404, '事项不存在')
                elif path == prefix + "/items":
                    text = values.get("title", [""])[0].strip()
                    if not text or len(text) > 200:
                        return self.send(400, "事项应为 1 到 200 字")
                    db.execute("INSERT INTO items(title) VALUES(?)", (text,))
                elif path.startswith(prefix + "/items/") and path.rsplit("/", 1)[1].isdigit():
                    done = values.get("done", [""])[0]
                    if done not in ("0", "1"):
                        return self.send(400, "状态不正确")
                    cur = db.execute("UPDATE items SET done=? WHERE id=?", (int(done), int(path.rsplit("/", 1)[1])))
                    if not cur.rowcount:
                        return self.send(404, "事项不存在")
                else:
                    return self.send(404, "页面不存在")
            self.send_response(303)
            self.send_header("Location", prefix + "/")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
            self.end_headers()

    return ThreadingHTTPServer(address, Handler)

import http.client
import json
import re
import sqlite3
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
from contextlib import contextmanager
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch
from urllib.parse import urlencode
from app import make_server


class Page(HTMLParser):
    """Read the controls a browser receives, including decoded attribute values."""

    def __init__(self, markup):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.forms = []
        self.controls = []
        self.links = []
        self.labels = []
        self.elements = []
        self.text = []
        self.form = None
        self.textarea = None
        self.textarea_first_data = False
        self.feed(markup)

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        attrs = dict(attrs)
        self.elements.append((tag, attrs))
        if tag == "form":
            self.form = {"action": attrs.get("action"),
                         "method": attrs.get("method", "get").lower(), "controls": []}
            self.forms.append(self.form)
        elif tag in ("input", "textarea"):
            control = dict(attrs)
            control.setdefault("value", "")
            self.controls.append(control)
            if self.form is not None:
                self.form["controls"].append(control)
            if tag == "textarea":
                self.textarea = control
                self.textarea_first_data = True
        elif tag == "a":
            self.links.append(attrs.get("href"))
        elif tag == "label":
            self.labels.append(attrs.get("for"))

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag == "form":
            self.form = None
        elif tag == "textarea":
            self.textarea = None

    def handle_data(self, data):
        self.text.append(data)
        if self.textarea is not None:
            if self.textarea_first_data:
                data = data[1:] if data.startswith("\n") else data
                self.textarea_first_data = False
            self.textarea["value"] += data


class ApplicationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.db = Path(self.tmp.name) / "app.db"
        self.prefix = "/demo"
        self.start()
        self.addCleanup(self.stop)

    def start(self, prefix=None):
        if prefix is not None:
            self.prefix = prefix
        self.server = make_server(("127.0.0.1", 0), self.db, self.prefix, "项目测试")
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever,
                                       kwargs={"poll_interval": 0.01}, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()

    def stop(self):
        if self.server is not None:
            self.server.shutdown()
            self.server.server_close()
            self.thread.join()
            self.server = None

    def call(self, method, path, data=None):
        status, _, body = self.call_response(method, path, data)
        return status, body

    def call_response(self, method, path, data=None):
        body = urlencode(data).encode("ascii") if data is not None else None
        return self.call_raw_response(method, path, body)

    def call_raw_response(self, method, path, body):
        conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", self.server.server_address[1], timeout=5)
        try:
            conn.request(method, path, body,
                         {"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"})
            r = conn.getresponse()
            headers = dict(r.getheaders())
            response = r.read()
            self.assertEqual(int(headers["Content-Length"]), len(response))
            return r.status, headers, response.decode("utf-8")
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def csrf(self):
        code, page = self.call("GET", self.prefix + "/")
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        return re.search('name="csrf" value="([^"]+)"', page)[1]

    def rows(self):
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db) as db:
            return db.execute("SELECT id,title,done FROM items ORDER BY id").fetchall()

    def create(self, title):
        self.assertEqual(self.call("POST", self.prefix + "/items",
                                   {"csrf": self.csrf(), "title": title})[0], 303)
        return self.rows()[-1][0]

    def edit_path(self, item_id):
        return self.prefix + "/items/%d/edit" % item_id

    def edit_form(self, page, item_id, title):
        parsed = Page(page)
        forms = [form for form in parsed.forms
                 if form["action"] == self.edit_path(item_id)]
        self.assertEqual(len(forms), 1, page)
        form = forms[0]
        self.assertEqual(form["method"], "post")
        fields = {control["name"]: control["value"] for control in form["controls"]
                  if "name" in control and "disabled" not in control}
        self.assertEqual(fields.get("title"), title)
        self.assertTrue(fields.get("csrf"))
        title_controls = [control for control in form["controls"]
                          if control.get("name") == "title"]
        self.assertEqual(len(title_controls), 1)
        self.assertIn(title_controls[0].get("id"), parsed.labels)
        self.assertIn(self.prefix + "/", parsed.links)
        return form["action"], fields

    def assert_safe_markup(self, page):
        for tag, attrs in Page(page).elements:
            self.assertNotEqual(tag, "script", page)
            self.assertFalse(any(name.lower().startswith("on") for name in attrs), page)

    def assert_retained_input(self, page, title):
        parsed = Page(page)
        self.assertIn(title, [control["value"] for control in parsed.controls
                              if control.get("name") == "title"])
        self.assertIn(self.prefix + "/", parsed.links)
        self.assert_safe_markup(page)

    @contextmanager
    def unavailable_database(self):
        backup = self.db.with_suffix(".backup")
        self.db.rename(backup)
        self.db.mkdir()
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            self.db.rmdir()
            backup.rename(self.db)

    def test_create_persist_and_complete(self):
        token = self.csrf()
        self.assertEqual(self.call("POST", "/demo/items", {"csrf": token, "title": "发布第一个版本"})[0], 303)
        self.assertIn("发布第一个版本", self.call("GET", "/demo/")[1])
        self.assertEqual(self.call("POST", "/demo/items/1", {"csrf": token, "done": "1"})[0], 303)
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db) as db:
            self.assertEqual(db.execute("SELECT title,done FROM items").fetchone(), ("发布第一个版本", 1))

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Codex desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Codex uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Codex calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Codex sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working but the person cannot see it.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Codex calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Codex opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Codex first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Codex desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). Codex then says what to do in the browser. Codex asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Codex also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, because the person may not have been watching the pane.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Codex completes persist for later. Codex treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Codex prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Codex loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Codex loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Codex prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Codex acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Codex waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Codex tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Codex calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Codex tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Codex starts itself, because those run where Codex's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Codex generated, Codex uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Codex desktop app on the person's computer while Codex runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Codex tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

from html.parser import HTMLParser

from app import make_server


class Page(HTMLParser):
    """Read the controls a browser receives, including decoded attribute values."""

    def __init__(self, markup):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.forms = []
        self.controls = []
        self.links = []
        self.labels = []
        self.elements = []
        self.text = []
        self.form = None
        self.textarea = None
        self.textarea_first_data = False
        self.feed(markup)

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        attrs = dict(attrs)
        self.elements.append((tag, attrs))
        if tag == "form":
            self.form = {"action": attrs.get("action"),
                         "method": attrs.get("method", "get").lower(), "controls": []}
            self.forms.append(self.form)
        elif tag in ("input", "textarea"):
            control = dict(attrs)
            control.setdefault("value", "")
            self.controls.append(control)
            if self.form is not None:
                self.form["controls"].append(control)
            if tag == "textarea":
                self.textarea = control
                self.textarea_first_data = True
        elif tag == "a":
            self.links.append(attrs.get("href"))
        elif tag == "label":
            self.labels.append(attrs.get("for"))

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag == "form":
            self.form = None
        elif tag == "textarea":
            self.textarea = None

    def handle_data(self, data):
        self.text.append(data)
        if self.textarea is not None:
            if self.textarea_first_data:
                data = data[1:] if data.startswith("\n") else data
                self.textarea_first_data = False
            self.textarea["value"] += data


class ApplicationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.db = Path(self.tmp.name) / "app.db"
        self.prefix = "/demo"
        self.start()
        self.addCleanup(self.stop)

    def start(self, prefix=None):
        if prefix is not None:
            self.prefix = prefix
        self.server = make_server(("127.0.0.1", 0), self.db, self.prefix, "项目测试")
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever,
                                       kwargs={"poll_interval": 0.01}, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()

    def stop(self):
        if self.server is not None:
            self.server.shutdown()
            self.server.server_close()
            self.thread.join()
            self.server = None

    def call(self, method, path, data=None):
        status, _, body = self.call_response(method, path, data)
        return status, body

    def call_response(self, method, path, data=None):
        body = urlencode(data).encode("ascii") if data is not None else None
        return self.call_raw_response(method, path, body)

    def call_raw_response(self, method, path, body):
        conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", self.server.server_address[1], timeout=5)
        try:
            conn.request(method, path, body,
                         {"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"})
            r = conn.getresponse()
            headers = dict(r.getheaders())
            response = r.read()
            self.assertEqual(int(headers["Content-Length"]), len(response))
            return r.status, headers, response.decode("utf-8")
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def csrf(self):
        code, page = self.call("GET", self.prefix + "/")
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        return re.search('name="csrf" value="([^"]+)"', page)[1]

    def rows(self):
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db) as db:
            return db.execute("SELECT id,title,done FROM items ORDER BY id").fetchall()

    def create(self, title):
        self.assertEqual(self.call("POST", self.prefix + "/items",
                                   {"csrf": self.csrf(), "title": title})[0], 303)
        return self.rows()[-1][0]

    def edit_path(self, item_id):
        return self.prefix + "/items/%d/edit" % item_id

    def edit_form(self, page, item_id, title):
        parsed = Page(page)
        forms = [form for form in parsed.forms
                 if form["action"] == self.edit_path(item_id)]
        self.assertEqual(len(forms), 1, page)
        form = forms[0]
        self.assertEqual(form["method"], "post")
        fields = {control["name"]: control["value"] for control in form["controls"]
                  if "name" in control and "disabled" not in control}
        self.assertEqual(fields.get("title"), title)
        self.assertTrue(fields.get("csrf"))
        title_controls = [control for control in form["controls"]
                          if control.get("name") == "title"]
        self.assertEqual(len(title_controls), 1)
        self.assertIn(title_controls[0].get("id"), parsed.labels)
        self.assertIn(self.prefix + "/", parsed.links)
        return form["action"], fields

    def assert_safe_markup(self, page):

    def test_oversized_edit_reads_bounded_chunks_and_handles_short_reads(self):
        item_id = self.create("分块前标题")
        before = self.rows()
        token = self.csrf()
        title = "字" * 1000 + '\n🙂\" & % + </textarea><script>alert(1)</script>\r\n'
        tail = urlencode([("title", title), ("csrf", token)]).encode("ascii")
        tail = tail.replace(b"title=", b"%74%69%74%6C%65=", 1)
        tail = tail.replace(b"csrf=", b"%63%73%72%66=", 1)
        # An encoded field name itself crosses the normal 8192-byte read boundary.
        padding_size = 8192 - len(b"padding=") - len(b"&") - 5
        encoded = b"padding=" + b"x" * padding_size + b"&" + tail
        self.assertGreater(len(encoded), 8192)
        requests = []
        handler_class = self.server.RequestHandlerClass
        original_setup = handler_class.setup

        class ShortReader:
            def __init__(self, stream):
                self.stream = stream

            def read(self, size=-1):
                requests.append(size)
                if not 0 < size <= 8192:
                    raise AssertionError("body reads must be positive and at most 8192 bytes")
                return self.stream.read(min(size, 17))

            def __getattr__(self, name):
                return getattr(self.stream, name)

        def setup_with_short_reader(handler):
            original_setup(handler)
            handler.rfile = ShortReader(handler.rfile)

        # First verify the encoded key crossing a full-size read, then exercise
        # short reads over the same HTTP request without replacing the transport.
        status, _, page = self.call_raw_response("POST", self.edit_path(item_id), encoded)
        self.assertEqual(status, 413)
        self.edit_form(page, item_id, title)
        with patch.object(handler_class, "setup", setup_with_short_reader):
            status, _, page = self.call_raw_response("POST", self.edit_path(item_id), encoded)
        self.assertEqual(status, 413)
        self.edit_form(page, item_id, title)
        self.assert_safe_markup(page)
        self.assertGreater(len(requests), 2)
        self.assertTrue(all(0 < size <= 8192 for size in requests))
        self.assertEqual(self.rows(), before)

        self.stop()
        self.start("/pv/BOOTV2/session")
        item_id = self.create("暂存失败不能改变原文")
        self.create("其他事项保持不变")
        before = self.rows()
        path = self.edit_path(item_id)
        submitted = [("title", "字" * 1000), ("csrf", self.csrf())]
        self.assertGreater(len(urlencode(submitted).encode("ascii")), 8192)
        real_temporary_file = tempfile.TemporaryFile

        class FailingTemporaryFile:
            def __init__(self, stream, stage):
                self.stream = stream
                self.stage = stage
                self.closed_event = threading.Event()

            def __enter__(self):
                self.stream.__enter__()
                return self

            def __exit__(self, *exc):
                try:
                    return self.stream.__exit__(*exc)
                finally:
                    self.closed_event.set()

            def write(self, data):
                if self.stage == "write":
                    self.stream.write(data[:4])
                    raise OSError("simulated temporary storage write failure")
                return self.stream.write(data)

            def flush(self):
                if self.stage == "flush":
                    raise OSError("simulated temporary storage flush failure")
                return self.stream.flush()

            def __getattr__(self, name):
                return getattr(self.stream, name)

        for stage in ("create", "write", "flush"):
            with self.subTest(failure=stage):
                created = []

                def failing_factory(*args, **kwargs):
                    if stage == "create":
                        raise OSError("simulated temporary storage creation failure")
                    resource = FailingTemporaryFile(real_temporary_file(*args, **kwargs), stage)
                    created.append(resource)
                    return resource

                with patch("app.tempfile.TemporaryFile", side_effect=failing_factory) as factory:
                    status, page = self.call("POST", path, submitted)
                factory.assert_called_once()
                self.assertEqual(status, 503)
                parsed = Page(page)
                self.assertIn("此次编辑未保存", "".join(parsed.text))
                self.assertIn("未能保留完整输入", "".join(parsed.text))
                self.assertIn(path, parsed.links)
                self.assertFalse(any(control.get("name") == "title" for control in parsed.controls))
                self.assert_safe_markup(page)
                self.assertEqual(self.rows(), before)
                self.assertEqual(len(created), 0 if stage == "create" else 1)
                for resource in created:
                    self.assertTrue(resource.closed_event.wait(timeout=1))
                    self.assertTrue(resource.stream.closed)

        elif tag in ("input", "textarea"):
            control = dict(attrs)
            control.setdefault("value", "")
            self.controls.append(control)
            if self.form is not None:
                self.form["controls"].append(control)
            if tag == "textarea":
                self.textarea = control
                self.textarea_first_data = True
        elif tag == "a":
            self.links.append(attrs.get("href"))
        elif tag == "label":
            self.labels.append(attrs.get("for"))
        elif tag == "script":
            self.script = {"attrs": attrs, "source": ""}
            self.scripts.append(self.script)

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag == "form":
            self.form = None
        elif tag == "textarea":
            self.textarea = None
        elif tag == "script":
            self.script = None

    def handle_data(self, data):
        self.text.append(data)
        if self.script is not None:
            self.script["source"] += data
        if self.textarea is not None:
            if self.textarea_first_data:
                data = data[1:] if data.startswith("\n") else data
                self.textarea_first_data = False

        if prefix is not None:

        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever,
                                       kwargs={"poll_interval": 0.01}, daemon=True)

        if self.server is not None:

    def call(self, method, path, data=None):
        status, _, body = self.call_response(method, path, data)
        return status, body

    def call_response(self, method, path, data=None, headers=None):
        body = urlencode(data).encode("ascii") if data is not None else None
        return self.call_raw_response(method, path, body, headers)

    def call_raw_response(self, method, path, body, headers=None):
        conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", self.server.server_address[1], timeout=5)
        try:
            request_headers = {"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"}
            request_headers.update(headers or {})
            conn.request(method, path, body, request_headers)
            return self.read_response(conn)
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def read_response(self, conn):
        response = conn.getresponse()
        headers = dict(response.getheaders())
        body = response.read()
        self.assertEqual(int(headers["Content-Length"]), len(body))
        return response.status, headers, body.decode("utf-8")

    def call_declared_body(self, path, size):
        """Send only headers: an oversized request must be rejected without a body."""
        conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", self.server.server_address[1], timeout=5)
        try:
            conn.putrequest("POST", path)
            conn.putheader("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
            conn.putheader("Content-Length", str(size))
            conn.endheaders()
            return self.read_response(conn)
        finally:
            conn.close()

# Codex in Chrome

Codex in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Codex in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Codex says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

If the only Codex in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Codex calls it first: it turns Codex in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.

## Loading the tools

If the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Codex loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:

```
ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"
```

Codex adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.

## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab

At the start of each browser session Codex calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:

1. Codex reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.
2. Otherwise Codex opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.
3. Codex never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Codex calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.

## Site permissions

Codex in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Codex tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Codex moves on.

## Recording a GIF

For multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Codex can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Codex captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example "login_process.gif").

## Reading console output

`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Codex is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern "[MyApp]" to keep only the application's own logs.

## Alerts and dialogs

Codex does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:

1. Codex avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a "Delete" button) unless necessary.
2. If it must interact with such an element, Codex warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.
3. Codex can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.

If a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Codex tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.

## Staying on task, and when to stop

Codex stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Codex stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:

- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts
- the extension gives no response
- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out
- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents
- several approaches have not completed the task

Codex does not keep retrying the same failing action.

# Computer use (desktop control)

Computer use lets Codex take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling, through the Codex desktop app. Its tools are named `mcp__computer-use__*` (for example `request_access`, `screenshot`) when the session runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__computer_*` (for example `computer_request_access`, `computer_screenshot`) when the session runs in the cloud and is linked to the person's computer. Computer use works only while Computer use is turned on in the Codex desktop app (Settings → This computer → Computer use; it is off by default).

## Turning computer use on from a chat

What Codex does first depends on which tools are present (loaded or deferred):

1. **Computer-use tools are present.** Codex goes straight to the access flow below.
2. **No computer-use tools, but an `enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer` tool is present.** Codex calls that tool once, before any other step of the task, with the task in its `task` field. When the call goes through, the `mcp__remote-devices__computer_*` tools arrive with it and Codex starts with the access flow below; there is no second enable step. If it does not go through, Codex relays the reason in one line and carries on with what it can do in the conversation.
3. **Neither.** Computer use is not available in this conversation as it stands, and Codex says so plainly without diagnosing why: in general Codex can use apps on a computer where the Codex desktop app is installed and signed in with Computer use turned on, and on Codex.ai in a web browser, if the composer's + menu offers Devices, the person can pick their computer there before sending a new message. Codex does not pretend to act.

## Separate filesystems

Computer-use actions (clicks, typing, clipboard writes) happen on the person's real computer, a different system from wherever Codex's own shell and files are, when it has them. Files Codex creates on its side do not exist on the person's machine. If Codex puts a command or file path in the person's clipboard, or types into one of their apps, the path must exist on their computer, not a path on Codex's side that they can't reach.

## Pick the right tool for the app

Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app**: if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, Codex uses it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Browser tools**: if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, Codex uses a browser: Codex in Chrome (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) or the built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` in the desktop app, `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer). Both are DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If this prompt has a `<browsers>` section, Codex follows it on which browser to use; otherwise it uses whichever one is connected. If neither is connected, Codex asks the person to connect one rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use**: for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use is the right tool here; Codex does not decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling: if a dedicated MCP tool errors, Codex debugs or reports it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

## Look before asserting

If the person asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), Codex takes a screenshot and checks before answering. Codex does not answer from memory: the person's setup or app version may differ from what it expects. If Codex is about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what it just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Codex loads them in bulk, not one-by-one: if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, Codex loads them all in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer", max_results: 40 }`. The keyword matches every computer-use tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit.

## Access flow

Before any computer-use action Codex must request access to the applications it needs: with the `mcp__computer-use__*` tools that is one `request_access` call with the list of applications; with the `mcp__remote-devices__computer_*` tools it is two calls, `computer_resolve_access` with the app names, then `computer_request_access` with the entries it returned, verbatim, and a one-sentence reason that explains the task. The person approves each application explicitly, and Codex may need to ask again mid-task if it discovers it needs another application. Codex waits for the person's answer rather than working around it.

## Tiered apps

Some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category; the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` (or `computer_request_access`) response:

- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. Codex can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, Codex uses Codex in Chrome (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) or the built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`, or `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when linked); it loads them via ToolSearch if deferred. If this prompt has a `<browsers>` section, Codex follows it on which browser to use; otherwise it uses whichever one is connected.
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. Codex can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, Codex uses its Bash tool when it has one.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells Codex what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier: bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

## Link safety

Codex treats links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.

- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If Codex encounters a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), it does not `left_click` it. It opens the URL via Codex in Chrome or the built-in browser instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading; Codex hovers or inspects to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, Codex asks the person for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside Codex in Chrome or the built-in browser** Codex can click links with those browser tools, but the suspicion check still applies: it verifies unfamiliar URLs with the person.

## Financial actions

Codex does not execute trades or move money. Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so Codex can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the person organize their finances. But Codex never executes a trade, places an order, sends money, or initiates a transfer on the person's behalf; it always asks the person to perform those actions themselves.

    def test_edit_request_body_reads_stay_within_recovery_budget(self):
        item_id = self.create("读取前标题")
        self.create("不应改变的另一行")
        token = self.csrf()
        title = "限额内更新"
        handler_class = self.server.RequestHandlerClass
        original_setup = handler_class.setup
        for size in (8192, 65536):
            with self.subTest(body_bytes=size):
                before = self.rows()
                submitted = [("title", title), ("csrf", token), ("padding", "")]
                base_size = len(urlencode(submitted).encode("ascii"))
                submitted[-1] = ("padding", "x" * (size - base_size))
                self.assertEqual(len(urlencode(submitted).encode("ascii")), size)
                requests, consumed = [], []

                class BudgetedReader:
                    def __init__(self, stream):
                        self.stream = stream

                    def read(self, requested=-1):
                        requests.append(requested)
                        if not 0 < requested <= 65536 or sum(consumed) + requested > 65536:
                            raise AssertionError("cumulative body reads must not exceed 65536 bytes")
                        data = self.stream.read(requested)
                        consumed.append(len(data))
                        return data

                    def __getattr__(self, name):
                        return getattr(self.stream, name)

                def setup_with_budget(handler):
                    original_setup(handler)
                    handler.rfile = BudgetedReader(handler.rfile)

                with patch.object(handler_class, "setup", setup_with_budget):
                    status, page = self.call("POST", self.edit_path(item_id), submitted)
                self.assertTrue(requests)
                self.assertEqual(sum(consumed), size)
                if size <= 8192:
                    self.assertEqual(status, 303)
                    self.assertEqual(self.rows(), [(i, title if i == item_id else text, done)
                                                   for i, text, done in before])
                else:
                    self.assertEqual(status, 413)
                    self.edit_form(page, item_id, title)
                    self.assertEqual(self.rows(), before)

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms

+class Page(HTMLParser):
+    """Read the controls a browser receives, including decoded attribute values."""

+    def __init__(self, markup):

+    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
+        attrs = dict(attrs)
+        self.elements.append((tag, attrs))
+        if tag == "form":
+            self.form = {"action": attrs.get("action"),
+                         "method": attrs.get("method", "get").lower(), "controls": []}
+            self.forms.append(self.form)
+        elif tag in ("input", "textarea"):
+            control = dict(attrs)
+            control.setdefault("value", "")
+            self.controls.append(control)
+            if self.form is not None:
+                self.form["controls"].append(control)
+            if tag == "textarea":
+                self.textarea = control
+                self.textarea_first_data = True
+        elif tag == "a":
+            self.links.append(attrs.get("href"))
+        elif tag == "label":
+            self.labels.append(attrs.get("for"))
+        elif tag == "script":
+            self.script = {"attrs": attrs, "source": ""}
+            self.scripts.append(self.script)
+
+    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
+        if tag == "form":
+            self.form = None
+        elif tag == "textarea":
+            self.textarea = None
+        elif tag == "script":
+            self.script = None
+
+    def handle_data(self, data):

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Codex desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Codex uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Codex calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Codex sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working but the person cannot see it.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Codex calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Codex opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Codex first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Codex desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). Codex then says what to do in the browser. Codex asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Codex also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, because the person may not have been watching the pane.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Codex completes persist for later. Codex treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Codex prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Codex loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Codex loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Codex prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Codex acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Codex waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Codex tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Codex calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Codex tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Codex starts itself, because those run where Codex's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Codex generated, Codex uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Codex desktop app on the person's computer while Codex runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Codex tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

# Computer use (desktop control)

Computer use lets Codex take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling, through the Codex desktop app. Its tools are named `mcp__computer-use__*` (for example `request_access`, `screenshot`) when the session runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__computer_*` (for example `computer_request_access`, `computer_screenshot`) when the session runs in the cloud and is linked to the person's computer. Computer use works only while Computer use is turned on in the Codex desktop app (Settings → This computer → Computer use; it is off by default).

## Turning computer use on from a chat

What Codex does first depends on which tools are present (loaded or deferred):

1. **Computer-use tools are present.** Codex goes straight to the access flow below.
2. **No computer-use tools, but an `enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer` tool is present.** Codex calls that tool once, before any other step of the task, with the task in its `task` field. When the call goes through, the `mcp__remote-devices__computer_*` tools arrive with it and Codex starts with the access flow below; there is no second enable step. If it does not go through, Codex relays the reason in one line and carries on with what it can do in the conversation.
3. **Neither.** Computer use is not available in this conversation as it stands, and Codex says so plainly without diagnosing why: in general Codex can use apps on a computer where the Codex desktop app is installed and signed in with Computer use turned on, and on Codex.ai in a web browser, if the composer's + menu offers Devices, the person can pick their computer there before sending a new message. Codex does not pretend to act.

## Separate filesystems

Computer-use actions (clicks, typing, clipboard writes) happen on the person's real computer, a different system from wherever Codex's own shell and files are, when it has them. Files Codex creates on its side do not exist on the person's machine. If Codex puts a command or file path in the person's clipboard, or types into one of their apps, the path must exist on their computer, not a path on Codex's side that they can't reach.

## Pick the right tool for the app

Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app**: if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, Codex uses it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Browser tools**: if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, Codex uses a browser: Codex in Chrome (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) or the built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` in the desktop app, `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer). Both are DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If this prompt has a `<browsers>` section, Codex follows it on which browser to use; otherwise it uses whichever one is connected. If neither is connected, Codex asks the person to connect one rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use**: for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use is the right tool here; Codex does not decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling: if a dedicated MCP tool errors, Codex debugs or reports it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

## Look before asserting

If the person asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), Codex takes a screenshot and checks before answering. Codex does not answer from memory: the person's setup or app version may differ from what it expects. If Codex is about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what it just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Codex loads them in bulk, not one-by-one: if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, Codex loads them all in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer", max_results: 40 }`. The keyword matches every computer-use tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit.

## Access flow

Before any computer-use action Codex must request access to the applications it needs: with the `mcp__computer-use__*` tools that is one `request_access` call with the list of applications; with the `mcp__remote-devices__computer_*` tools it is two calls, `computer_resolve_access` with the app names, then `computer_request_access` with the entries it returned, verbatim, and a one-sentence reason that explains the task. The person approves each application explicitly, and Codex may need to ask again mid-task if it discovers it needs another application. Codex waits for the person's answer rather than working around it.

## Tiered apps

Some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category; the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` (or `computer_request_access`) response:

- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. Codex can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, Codex uses Codex in Chrome (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) or the built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`, or `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when linked); it loads them via ToolSearch if deferred. If this prompt has a `<browsers>` section, Codex follows it on which browser to use; otherwise it uses whichever one is connected.
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. Codex can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, Codex uses its Bash tool when it has one.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells Codex what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier: bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

## Link safety

Codex treats links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.

- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If Codex encounters a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), it does not `left_click` it. It opens the URL via Codex in Chrome or the built-in browser instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading; Codex hovers or inspects to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, Codex asks the person for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside Codex in Chrome or the built-in browser** Codex can click links with those browser tools, but the suspicion check still applies: it verifies unfamiliar URLs with the person.

## Financial actions

Codex does not execute trades or move money. Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so Codex can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the person organize their finances.
